<!-- pr-reviewer: 78498c040ee424fd0376a219b572bda7e6e1279b -->
**Ready for the maintainer to merge.** No blockers.

**What looks good**
- `path_sig.rs` hashes endpoints, feed and arc centre through `cl::lattice`, the very function `MoveDto::from_move` calls on save (`crates/app/src/project/entity.rs:455-466`): same step (1e6), same `round()` (half away from zero), same handling of negatives and -0.0 (identical call on both sides, so identical bits). Non-finite values pass through untouched, no panic. `lattice` is idempotent on stored values, so save-load-save agrees.
- (b) The comparison stays exact on snapped values. Only sub-half-micron differences now hash equal, which is exactly the difference a saved file cannot carry. Only consumer of `path_sig::of` is `Toolpath::new` (`schema.rs:415`); lathe-body cache and fixture view key on that stamp, and no file or post can tell such paths apart, so a reused cache cannot differ in anything that is written or posted. A 1 um change still moves the signature (pinned).
- (c) Already-on-grid values hash bit-for-bit as before, no hash-prefix change, so existing stamps still match.
- (d) No unwrap/expect/panic added.
- (g) `docs/decisions/1351-path-sig-lattice.md` present; body has `Changelog:` and `Fixes #1351`.

**Local results (merged with main)**
| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `turning_thread` | 10 passed |
| pinning test on origin/main's `path_sig.rs` | fails (`left: 6467650602549402493, right: 17772775613656745229`); passes with the fix (e) |
| `float_roundtrip` / `project_roundtrip` / `rest_across_setups` | 3 / 73 / 7 passed |
| `clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -D warnings` | clean |

**Notes (not blocking)**
1. (f) `crates/app/tests/turning_thread.rs` is 447 lines (416 on main, +31 here). It was already over the ~400 rule; growth of an already-over file is a note, not a blocker. A follow-up could move the save/load chain test into its own file.
2. The signature still does not hash `axis`/`rotary` (unchanged behaviour, outside this issue).

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
